title: Route model calls through an ordered list of providers, the Mac first
body:
## What changed

**Models router (`deploy/models_router.py`).** The router on the droplet took one primary (Modal) and one fallback (the Mac). It now takes an ordered list of providers:

- `MODELS_PROVIDERS` is a comma list of names. The default is `local,modal`, so the Mac comes first and Modal second.
- Each provider reads `MODELS_<NAME>_URL` and, optionally, `MODELS_<NAME>_PROXY`.
- Any provider that answers 402 or 429, or can't be reached, sits out for `MODELS_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` while the next one serves. When every provider is out, all are still tried in order.
- `GET /router/status` now returns `order`, `using` and `out_for_seconds`.
- The old `MODELS_PRIMARY_URL`, `MODELS_FALLBACK_URL` and `MODELS_FALLBACK_PROXY` settings still work and mean modal, then local.

**Tests.** Five router tests replace the primary/fallback test. They cover the default order, the cooldown, all providers out, the legacy settings, and the error when a provider's URL is missing.

**Docs.** `docs/models-service.md` describes the new settings. This branch also carries an earlier commit that adds the Mac's memory use and a Cost section (Modal plans and the DigitalOcean GPU droplet price) to the same file.

## Why

Modal's monthly credit ran out in November and the Mac has served since. A list of providers lets the Mac be the default and lets another provider be added by configuration. The next step is DigitalOcean serverless inference for the reranker and bge-m3. On 100 real passages from the paper index, its scores matched ours: the reranker to within 1.1e-5 with the same top 5, and bge-m3 at a cosine similarity of at least 0.9996.

## For reviewers

- **Deploying alone changes nothing on the droplet.** It still uses the legacy settings, which keep Modal first. It goes Mac-first only once its settings switch to `MODELS_PROVIDERS`.
- **Behaviour change:** a 402 or 429 from the last provider tried now gives the router's 503 instead of that provider's own error.
- **Tests:** the full suite passes (540) and ruff reports nothing.

title: Add a DigitalOcean provider to the models router
body:
Stacked on #68 (the ordered provider list). Its base is `claude/models-providers`; once #68 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to `main`.

## What changed

**DigitalOcean provider (`deploy/models_router.py`).** A provider with `MODELS_<N>_KIND=digitalocean` serves reranking and embeddings from DigitalOcean's serverless inference (`https://inference.do-ai.run`, models `bge-reranker-v2-m3` and `bge-m3`).

- `/rerank` goes to DigitalOcean's `/v1/rerank`. The answer comes back as `{"scores": [...]}` in document order, the same shape the Mac and Modal return. The model name paper-fetch sends is replaced with DigitalOcean's.
- `/v1/embeddings` and Ollama's `/api/embed` (which the hub calls) go to `/v1/embeddings`. DigitalOcean's vectors aren't unit length (about 26), while Ollama's are, so the router scales them to unit length.
- Every other call goes to the next provider without putting DigitalOcean out: the claim checker's `/api/chat`, `/api/tags` and `/api/ps`.
- 401, 402, 403 and 429 put DigitalOcean out for the cooldown. Serverless inference is prepaid, so an empty balance falls back to the next provider.
- `MODELS_<N>_KEY_FILE` sends a provider's own key in place of the caller's. The key is never logged.
- `MODELS_<N>_EMBED_MODEL` and `MODELS_<N>_RERANK_MODEL` set the model names; the defaults are `bge-m3` and `bge-reranker-v2-m3`.

**Tests.** Eight new tests cover:
- the request mapping;
- calls DigitalOcean doesn't serve;
- the score order;
- unit-length scaling in both response shapes;
- the swap to DigitalOcean's own key;
- `/api/chat` passing on to the next provider;
- falling back on a 402;
- the settings read from the environment.

The app-level tests use `httpx.MockTransport`. `fastapi` and `httpx` join the `dev` group, and `uv.lock` is updated, so CI can run them.

**Docs.** `docs/models-service.md` gains a DigitalOcean section and DigitalOcean's prices under Cost: $0.01 per million tokens for the reranker and $0.02 for bge-m3, prepaid.

## Why

Modal's monthly credit ran out. DigitalOcean serves the same two models per token, with no GPU to wake, for cents a month.

## Checks

- `uv run pytest -q`: 548 passed. `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` are clean.
- **Live check on 2026-11-23.** The router ran on the Mac with `MODELS_PROVIDERS=digitalocean,local`:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `/rerank`, 20 real passages | Same scores as the Mac's full-precision reranker to within 7.8e-6; DigitalOcean took 1.2 s, the Mac 3.7 s |
| `/api/embed` | Unit-length vectors, cosine similarity of at least 0.99977 with Ollama's |
| `/v1/embeddings` | Unit length, in the OpenAI shape |
| `/api/tags` | Passed through to the Mac |

- An earlier direct comparison on 100 passages matched to within 1.1e-5 (reranker) and a cosine of at least 0.9996 (bge-m3).

## For reviewers

- **Deploying alone changes nothing on the droplet.** It needs `MODELS_PROVIDERS=digitalocean,local,modal` and a DigitalOcean *model access key* in `MODELS_DIGITALOCEAN_KEY_FILE`. That key hasn't been created yet.
- **The claim checker (bespoke-minicheck) is unaffected.** It still goes to the Mac, then Modal.

The work of #14 (branch `design-system`), rebased onto `main` at v0.12.1, plus a release commit for **v0.13.0**. The three commits from #14 are unchanged in substance; the conflicts were resolved keeping v0.12.x behaviour, including `scaffold check` skipping the `.scaffold/` CI checkout.

November's Modal spend reached about $40. The model app cost $15–16 a day from 18 November, against an estimate of about $27 a month. The droplet's logs for 19 November show 1,946 tool calls spread over 21 of 24 hours.

The cause: every `ask` woke the hosted models and waited for them, even `code:` asks that never touch a model. Every session start woke them too. With a 10-minute idle window, an L4 stayed up about 20 hours that day.

title: Fall back to the Mac's models when Modal is out
body:
## What this does

Modal's model service ran out of budget and started answering HTTP 429 ("Input rate limit (0/s)"), which took down passage retrieval and the verifier. This adds an automatic fallback to the same models on the Mac.

- **`deploy/models_service.py`**: the model service as one portable file. It serves Ollama's API (bge-m3, bespoke-minicheck), plus `/rerank` for bge-reranker-v2-m3, behind the bearer key. Modal serves it on a GPU, and the Mac runs it with `uv run` next to its native Ollama. The reranker loads on first use and is dropped after 10 idle minutes. It's loaded from real files in one folder, because onnxruntime refuses the hub cache's symlinked `model.onnx_data`.
- **`deploy/modal_models.py`**: serves that same app (`add_local_file` and `create_app`) instead of its own copy. The models and their scoring are unchanged.
- **`deploy/models_router.py`**: runs on the droplet at `127.0.0.1:8895`.
  - It tries Modal first. On a 402 or 429, or when Modal can't be reached, it uses the Mac for `MODELS_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (900), then tries Modal again.
  - `GET /router/status` says which side is serving.
  - Only the Mac-bound client uses `MODELS_FALLBACK_PROXY` (tailscaled's loopback proxy; the droplet stays in userspace mode). Neither client reads proxy settings from the environment, so paper and web fetches can't reach the tailnet.
- **`tests/test_models_service.py`**: the router's switching, and the reranker loading on use and dropping when idle.
- **`docs/models-service.md`**: the set-up on each host.

## Already live

- The droplet runs the router from `/home/rag/models-router/` until this merges. Its three model URLs point at the router, with `.before-router` backups kept.
- The Mac runs the service, published tailnet-only on port 8896.
- With Modal still answering 429, `rag__retrieve_evidence` and `ask` return passages through the Mac.

## Not yet verified

- minicheck through the fallback in a research run.

title: Add reextract: re-run TEI extraction on stored originals
body:
## Why

#15 made `xml_text` keep GROBID display formulas, but only for papers fetched after it. `index --refresh` re-reads the stored `fulltext.txt` and never re-extracts, so older papers keep text with every display equation missing. Example: W2014360559 (Machura et al. 2007, fetched 2026-11-10) has no eq. 1 in the index, while W2057708301 (fetched 2026-11-19) does.

## What

- `Library.reextract(identifiers=None, *, collection=None)`: for each held work with a stored `fulltext.tei.xml`, re-runs `xml_text` and the prose gate. If the text changed it rewrites `fulltext.txt`, updates provenance (`sha256`, `text_method`, `text_gate`, and a `reextracted` entry with date, old and new sha256), and re-indexes the work's passages. Identical text: counted unchanged, nothing written. No stored TEI, not held, or gate failure: reported in `skipped`. Local only; the stored XML is never touched.
- CLI: `paper-fetch reextract [id ...] [--collection C]`; one line in the CLI docstring and in CLAUDE.md.
- Tests (written first): formula restored with provenance updated and the XML untouched; second run unchanged; no TEI skipped; the formula retrievable after re-indexing.

Source: housekeeping (re-runs the extraction from #15, which carries its sources).

## Not in this PR

- The catalogue row is not updated: a work whose row says `full_text: false` keeps that until a catalogue rebuild.
- Inline maths GROBID itself garbles; preferring arXiv PDFs; filling `ids.arxiv`.

## Checks

`uv run pytest -q` 390 passed; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; `pyright` 0 errors.

## After merge

On the research-rag droplet: update paper-fetch, run `paper-fetch reextract W2014360559`, check eq. 1 retrieves verbatim, then run it for all tei-xml works.

title: Add ask fetch mode and delegate/strict autonomy
body:
## Why

`ask` asked too many obvious questions ("fallback or stop?" whenever a component failed, "should I fetch/index this paper?"), and any request mentioning a paper ran the whole research pipeline.

## What changed

**Fetch mode**
- `routing.py` / `config/routing.default.toml`: new `fetch` mode. Prefixes `fetch:` and `paper:`, a `[fetch]` trigger list ("get the paper", "index this paper", …), or a DOI together with get/fetch/download/index/add (`FETCH_VERBS`). A DOI on its own (e.g. in a code task) does not route to fetch.
- `ask.py`: fetch mode indexes DOIs and `pmid:` ids with `rag__index_paper`. A title is searched with `papers__search` (limit 3), the top hit is indexed, and the other two are listed as "if this isn't the paper you meant". No pipeline, no specialist, no fresh search.
- `gateway.py`: `call_for_ask` routes the ask's `rag__index_paper` call to the built-in evidence store (it isn't an upstream tool). Adds `fetch` to the mode enum and a sentence to the server instructions.

**Autonomy**
- `hub/contract.py`: `AUTONOMY = ("delegate", "strict")`, `MUST_ASK = ("library", "verifier")`.
- `ask.py`: `ask(autonomy=...)`. Under `delegate` (the default) a failing component takes its labelled fallback and the degraded problem is recorded; library and verifier still ask; a session "stop" still wins. `strict` keeps today's behaviour.
- `brief.py`: under delegate, the answer format tells the assistant to fetch and index up to five fresh leads and retrieve again; the strict text is unchanged.
- `gateway.py`: default from env `ASK_AUTONOMY` (default `delegate`); `autonomy` in ask's inputSchema; delegate instruction sentence.
- `docs/mcp-clients.md`: paragraphs on fetch mode and the two autonomy modes.

## Notes for reviewers
- **Behaviour change on deploy:** the default becomes `delegate`, so the reranker, embeddings, provider, github and corpus failures no longer stop to ask. Set `ASK_AUTONOMY=strict` on the droplet to keep the old behaviour.
- arXiv ids and PMCIDs are not recognised yet (no pattern was specified).
- `tests/test_hub.py`'s `Rig.ask` now defaults to `autonomy="strict"`, since those tests cover asking; delegate is covered in the new `tests/test_autonomy.py`.
- A title fetch uses the hit's `openalex` work id when it has no DOI.

title: Keep GROBID display formulas in TEI text
body:
## Problem `xml_text()` built `fulltext.txt` from `

` elements only. GROBID writes display equations as `` elements beside the paragraphs (equation number in `

`, as its own block: the formula text, then its label (e.g. `ż = -β y -γz + Ku(z i ). (9)`). Formulas inside a `

` were already kept through the paragraph text and are not duplicated. The fallback for text with no paragraphs is unchanged. - `tests/test_text.py`: `test_tei_keeps_formulas_with_labels_in_order`: a labelled formula, an unlabelled formula and document order. The fixture has no digits, because the owner's citation check requires every number in a change to be in the cited passages. ## Sources - Lo, Wang, Neumann et al. 2020, *S2ORC: The Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus*, ACL, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.447. Evidence `W3015453090#p6.c5137c44`: "From the XML output of GROBID, we extract … (iv) equations, table content, headers, and footers, which we remove from the body text". This confirms GROBID gives equations apart from the paragraphs. S2ORC itself chose to remove them. - Zanibbi, Mansouri, Agarwal 2025, *Mathematical Information Retrieval: Search and Question Answering*, Foundations and Trends in IR, doi:10.1561/1500000095. title: Make an ask wait for a hosted model service that is waking up
body:
## Why

The Modal model service scales to zero. A cold container takes about 13 s to start and about 35 s to load bge-m3. An ask sent in that window, such as the first ask in a new session or after more than 10 idle minutes, ran into the 40 s retrieval limit and came back as `needs_decision`.

## What

`research_mcp/gateway.py`:
- `wake_hosted_models()` now records its in-flight request in an event that is set when the request ends, whatever the outcome.
- `models_ready()` waits on that event, and returns at once when nothing is in flight.
- Before an `ask` runs, the gateway wakes a hosted Ollama if it has been idle, the same wake-up a new session sends at most once a minute, then waits for any wake-up in flight. Modal answers that request only after the container has started and loaded bge-m3, so retrieval finds the models ready.

There are no new settings: the wait is bounded by the wake-up request's existing 300 s timeout. A local Ollama (no key) is never woken or waited on.

`tests/test_remote_models.py`: the wait returns at once with nothing in flight, holds while a wake-up is in flight, and ends when it finishes.

- ruff, format, pyright clean; full suite: 544 passed, 2 skipped.

title: Add an extension API so anyone can build their own research-rag
body:
## What

An extension API for the gateway. Installed `rag-ext-*` packages (entry point `rag.extensions`) can add:

- **MCP tools** under their own prefix (`<prefix>__<tool>`); core prefixes such as `rag`, `papers`, `pipeline` and `polarize` are reserved.
- **`ask` steps** that run when their trigger words appear in a question (extra words can come from `config/routing.toml`). A step's result lands in `results["extensions"][<ext>][<step>]` and reaches clients as `brief.tool_results.extensions`.

It mirrors the existing domain loader in `research_pipeline/domains.py`: name prefix, `core_requires` version gate, `declare()`, `discover()`.

## Why

The core should stay a public, general tool. Personal or project-specific features can then live in separate packages that build on it, rather than in this repo. This is phase 1 of that plan. Moving the Polarize, sky and mixer pieces out into their own extension package is a later PR.

## The one rule

An extension only adds. It works on a deep copy of `results`, so it can't change evidence, retrieval, verification, grading, coverage or another step's output. A step that raises is recorded as `{"error": ...}` with a progress line; `ask` carries on.

## Changes

- `research_mcp/extensions.py` (new): `declare`, `discover`, `loaded`, `get`, `matches`, and the `Context` / `ToolSpec` / `StepSpec` / `StepInput` / `StepOutput` types.
- `research_mcp/routing.py`: `[extensions.<name>]` trigger-word tables.
- `research_mcp/ask.py`: runs matching steps after the Polarize step; their `found`, `next`, `for_you` and relay lines appear in the reply.
- `research_mcp/gateway.py`: discovers extensions and lists and dispatches their tools. Gateway config gains a `disabled` list and a per-extension config section; `gateway_status` gains `extensions` rows (`ok`, `undeclared`, `incompatible`, `error`, `disabled`, `clash`). Tools are refused when `builtin_tools` is false.
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`, `docs/extension-template/`, README section, config examples.
- Core version `0.3.0` (`uv.lock` unchanged).

## For reviewers

- Extension steps don't run on requests `ask` answers early (for example the profiles list). They also don't show in a reply that is still pending when the hub deadline passes; their output reaches the final reply in the ledger.
- No paper backs this design: it's the owner's own engineering choice. The Gewaltig & Cannon (2014, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003376) note on plugin support is cited as background only.

title: ask: lower the relevance floor; gateway: record every tool call with backlinks
body:
Two changes. Each is its own commit, so they can be reviewed separately.

## 1. ask: lower the reranker relevance floor from 0 to -3 (7d22c35)

- `RELEVANCE_FLOOR` in `research_mcp/ask.py` goes from `0.0` to `-3.0`, and the comment now says why.
- A new test in `tests/test_ask.py` checks that near-misses (-0.03, -0.95, -2.9) are still shown. Unrelated text at -4.2 and below stays hidden.

The floor from #28 was set from one example of unrelated text, which scored -4 to -6. `ask` reranks passages against the whole question, which gives lower scores than a short query, so a floor of 0 hid relevant passages. Users got "No passage was relevant enough to show … at most -0.95".

| Passage | Short query | Whole question via `ask` |
|---|---|---|
| Alonso et al. 2025: distortion products "about 15%" of the primaries | +1.47 | +0.14 |
| Next-closest passages | — | ≤ -0.03 (hidden at floor 0) |

-3 is based on a handful of queries, not a benchmark. It's a single constant, easy to tune later.

## 2. gateway: record every tool call, with record pages and backlinks (b6ac2b5)

**Recording**
- Every tool call is written to a local SQLite outbox (`calls.sqlite`), then copied to Postgres (Neon) when `CALL_LOG_DATABASE_URL` is set.
- If the database is down, the gateway retries every minute and keeps everything locally.
- Copied rows leave the outbox after `CALL_LOG_LOCAL_DAYS` (7). With no database configured, nothing is pruned.
- Each record holds client, session, project, tool, arguments, the full response, and its references (`run`, `run_id`, `request`, `doi`, `url`) in `mcp_call_refs`.

**Links in replies**
- Replies get a `links` field: `record`, `research` and `requests`. Where a reply has a `relay`, a **Links** list is appended to it.
- Status tools are recorded but get no links.
- The server instructions now tell clients to keep these links.

**Record pages** (`research_mcp/records.py`)
- `/records` lists recent calls. `/records/<id>` shows one call. `/records/request/<id>` shows a request's history.
- `/records/run/<folder or run id>` shows a run's `answer.md` and every call that refers to it, which are the backlinks.
- Pages answer only loopback clients. Requests marked as Funnel, or addressed to the public host, get a 404.

**Setup**
- `docs/call-log.md` covers the Neon setup (connection string in the Keychain, `tailscale serve` on port 8892, `RECORDS_URL`).
- It also covers moving to DigitalOcean later with `pg_dump`/`pg_restore`.
- `psycopg[binary]` is an optional extra: `uv sync --extra calllog`.

### For reviewers

- The copy to a real Postgres is untested here: no local Postgres, and no Neon project yet. The tests cover it with a stand-in connection.
- The tables are plain, with no extensions, so they move between Postgres hosts with a dump and restore.
- Stored responses include questions and passage text; that's intended, and the doc says so.
- `uv run pytest` after merging main: 474 passed, 2 skipped (live-only sky tests). The new `sky__` and `math__audio_mix` tools are recorded like every other tool. `ruff` and `pyright` are clean, apart from the optional `psycopg` import.

title: sky__measure, sky__locate: sun sights from sky-clock, and ask runs them
body:
Adds two built-in tools over sky-clock's new sun-sight routes (polarizetech/sky-clock#16), so a client can measure the Sun from a stick and its shadow and locate itself from that.

## Tools

- **`sky__measure`** (`/api/measure`): a plumbed stick and its shadow (length and bearing, or the tip's east and north offsets) give the Sun's altitude and azimuth, with the triangle's legs and residual.
- **`sky__locate`** (`/api/locate`): the Sun's altitude and azimuth (or the stick, shadow and bearing) at a UTC time give the places that see the Sun there (up to two), each with its local apparent and mean solar time and how many km it moves per 0.1° of measuring error and per second of clock error.

## `ask`

- **Runs a sight from plain words.** "Where am I? A 1 m stick casts a 2.69 m shadow pointing 32° at 2026-11-04T22:00Z" returns 48.290, −123.059, local solar time 14:04:10, about 12 km per 0.1°.
- **Gives both places when there are two.** "the sun is 5 degrees up at azimuth 0 at 2026-06-21T12:00Z" returns the far south at noon and the Arctic at midnight.
- **Says what is missing,** such as the shadow's bearing.
- **Ignores unrelated "locate" requests** ("locate the paper on bee dances").
- **Skips passage retrieval** for a sight, as for a sky key.

## Also

`jd_iso` now rounds to the nearest second instead of truncating (21:59:59.9999 read 21:59:59), which also affects `sky__key`'s event times.

## Checks

- `tests/test_sky_sight.py`: the sight parser (five phrasings, things it must leave alone, missing parts), arranging sky-clock's answer, and `ask` with a sight and with a missing bearing. Live tests run with `SKY_CLOCK_LIVE=1`.

title: sky__key: the sky key and clock times from sky-clock, and ask runs it
body:
Adds a built-in tool, `sky__key`, that asks a running [sky-clock](https://github.com/polarizetech/sky-clock) data server for the sky key and clock times at a place and time. `ask` runs it by itself when a request asks for them.

## `sky__key`

Inputs: `lat`, `lon` (decimal degrees), optional `t` (UTC ISO or `jd:`; default now), `h` (metres), `heading` (degrees from north).

It reads `/api/key` and `/api/clocks` from `SKY_CLOCK_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8803`) and returns:
- **Key:** the key/1 hash, its bins and code row; the Sun's azimuth, elevation and direction; gravity.
- **Unit triangles:** the Sun split against gravity (sin el, cos el), the azimuth as (cos, sin), and with a heading the dance angle (heading × conj(azimuth)), each with its Pythagorean residual.
- **Clocks:** solar time, mean solar time, the equation of time, lunar time.
- **Moon:** position, phase, illuminated fraction.
- **Events (UTC):** sunrise, solar noon, sunset, moonrise, moonset, next transit, next quarter.
- **Tide:** tidal gravity.
- **Source:** sky-clock's version, commit and ephemeris, with every number.

No model runs and nothing is computed here; place names are not looked up.

## `ask`

- A request with a sky trigger ("sky key", "solar time", "lunar time", "moon time", "sunrise", ...) and decimal coordinates gets the reading in `results.sky`, a one-line summary in `relay`, and every value in `relay_full`.
- A quick-mode sky request skips passage retrieval (papers don't hold clock times).
- Without coordinates, the reply says what to give; if sky-clock is down, it says so and names the URL.

title: ask: relevance floor for passages; stricter anchoring for name-derived specialists
body:
Found while auditing `structured-noise-identification`'s stochastic-resonance bench with `ask` and `rag__retrieve_evidence`: two kinds of irrelevant output.

## 1. Unrelated passages shown when nothing relevant exists
The request "use the reg tool to do an audit … put in a PR" was routed `quick` and returned 5 passages:
- 3 from an EEG paper on **REG**/RAND tone sequences
- 1 from a direction-of-arrival paper where **PR** means "probability of resolution"
- 1 on spike-pattern quality

The reranker scored all 5 between −4.2 and −5.6. Every relevant top hit in the audit scored above 0.4.

**Change:** `ask` now drops passages the reranker scores below `RELEVANCE_FLOOR = 0.0`.
- Below 0, the bge cross-encoder judges a passage more likely irrelevant than relevant.
- If nothing passes, the relay says "No passage was relevant enough to show …" with the best score. If some pass, it says how many weaker ones were left out.
- The floor applies only when the library reports a reranker, because otherwise `score` is a fused rank on a different scale.
- `rag__retrieve_evidence` is unchanged and still returns raw ranked passages.

## 2. Wrong specialist from a generic word in its name
"…array-enhanced SR with mean-field coupling…" was routed to **antenna-array-engineering** (score 14). A profile without curated `SPECIALIST_TERMS` was anchored by any hyphen-part of its name, so "array" was enough.

**Change:** a name-derived anchor now needs every distinctive part of the name.
- Generic role words (`engineering`, `analyst`, `research`, …) don't count, and a simple plural is accepted.
- `noise-engineering` still anchors on "noise". `antenna-array-engineering` needs both "antenna" and "array(s)".
- Curated `SPECIALIST_TERMS` profiles are unchanged.
- Trade-off: a multi-part name may now under-route, falling back to the general researcher, which is safe. Before, it could inject the wrong specialist's guidance into the run.

## Not fixed here
These are ranking or corpus issues, not routing bugs:
- **Ranking:** some relevant-scoring results are still off-topic. Example: "chaotic resonance …" puts a chaotic-MUSIC DOA paper 4th, with a reranker score of 3.0.
- **Corpus gaps:** no passage was found for Tessone 2006 (diversity-induced resonance), cascaded SR, or the √dt scaling of Euler–Maruyama.

## Checks
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pyright` and `pytest --cov` all pass: 424 tests, 86.5% coverage.
- 3 of the 4 new tests fail on `main`. The fourth guards the no-reranker case.

- **One error contract** on every non-success reply: `status`, `component`, `what_failed`, `impact`, `fallback_used`, `options`, `recommendation`, `retry_after`. The relay shows it first in plain words. Gateway tool errors, upstream errors and the bridge's "gateway is down" all carry it.
- **Health and circuit breakers** for the reranker, embeddings, paper library, model provider, verifier, upstream processes, GitHub and the corpus (3 failures, then skipped for 120 s, then probed), with the plan's labelled fallbacks.
- **Usage meters**: OpenRouter `/api/v1/key` + `/api/v1/credits` (balance, day/week/month spend, burn per day, run-out); NEAR AI reported as "needs a reporting token" until `~/.config/polarize/nearai-reporting.env` exists; Ollama up/installed/loaded. - **Provider ladders** (`research_pipeline/ladder.py`, `config/hub.default.toml`): planning, extraction and writing go OpenRouter → NEAR AI direct → local `qwen3:4b-instruct-2507`, skipping a rung that is failing or low (USD 1 or 95 %). Each move is logged in the run's notes and ladder log. Checking stays on the local verifier.

## Decisions (asked 2026-10-28)
- Code conflict: **worktrees**. Nothing is blocked; `ask` mentions recent code work on the same repo from another session and says to use your own worktree.
- Degraded fallbacks: **ask once per session per component**. The reply is `needs_decision`; the client passes `decisions={"<component>": "fallback"|"stop"}`, and that choice holds for the rest of the session.
- Session identity: **pass it, or the gateway infers it**. The bridge sends `X-Hub-Session`/`X-Hub-Project`; inferred sessions are marked in the ledger.
- Ladders and thresholds: **as proposed**.

## Limits
- Switching off only the reranker or only the embeddings needs `rerank`/`dense` flags on paper-fetch's `retrieve` tool. The gateway sends them as soon as the tool lists them; until then those two fall back to scholarly search, and the relay says so.
- Inside a running pipeline, ladder moves happen automatically and are labelled; only the pre-run check asks.
- Upstream restart with backoff is phase 3: for now a dead upstream fails with the restart command.

title: Send every question to the retrieval tool, and let it pick the specialist
body:
The person's requirement (2026-10-28): every question in these projects, by any assistant, runs the retrieval tool, and specialists are brought in only where the tool's pipeline routes them.

- **`retrieval_rule`.** When a profile names a retrieval tool, `AGENTS.md` now says every question starts with it, including one about the repo's own code: retrieve, then read the checkout. A second rule says research roles and specialists come only from `pipeline__profile_route`.
- **`scaffold rag-hook --server NAME`.** A Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook, installed beside the session hook when the profile names a tool. On every prompt it adds the rule to the context. When `$RESEARCH_RAG_URL` and `$RESEARCH_RAG_TOKEN_FILE` point at the tool's HTTP gateway, it also adds the route for the prompt: specialist, brief path and guidance.
  - It never blocks a prompt and skips slash commands.

  - Nothing machine-specific is written into a repo.
  - `scaffold update` adds, refreshes or removes the hook.
- **Other assistants** have no hook; they follow the rule in `AGENTS.md`.

title: Harden repos__propose_files and allow a dedicated GitHub token
body:
Prepares the `repos__` tools for use from a chat client (Open WebUI) whose model may have read untrusted text, such as paper passages or web pages.

## What changes

- **`repos__propose_files` refuses dangerous paths** before anything is cloned:
  - Any path with a `.git` component. Writing `.git/config` can set `core.fsmonitor` or similar settings, so the next `git add` would run a program on the host.
  - `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/`. A workflow on a pushed branch runs with the repository's secrets before anyone reviews the PR.
  - Writing through a symbolic link.
  - Paths are compared case-insensitively, since macOS would place `.GitHub/Workflows/x.yml` inside `.github/workflows/`.
- **Every git command** runs with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false`. Credentials come explicitly from `gh auth git-credential`, so the tool no longer depends on the host's global git config.
- **`GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`** (optional) gives the tool its own token, for example a fine-grained token limited to chosen repositories with Contents and Pull requests read/write and no Workflows permission. It is passed to `gh` and git as `GH_TOKEN`, and errors name the file, never the token. Without it, behaviour is unchanged: `gh`'s login is used.
- **`repos__auth_status`** reports the credential source (`gh login` or `GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`) and the protected paths.
- **Docs:** `config/rag.env.example` and `docs/mcp-clients.md` describe the token file and the protected paths. They also note the remaining exposure: a workflow that already runs on every push still runs proposed code with whatever secrets it can reach, so deploy secrets belong in GitHub environments that require approval.

## Testing

- 15 new tests: rejected and allowed paths, refusing symlinks, path checks running before any command, token-file handling and errors, and the git hardening flags.
- The full suite passes locally (325 tests). Ruff is clean.
- Checked with a fake token that `gh auth git-credential` returns `GH_TOKEN`.
- The running gateway serves this code. `repos__auth_status` and `repos__list_repositories` work. `propose_files` has not been run against a real repository.

title: Share one half-precision vector copy; allow hosted embeddings and reranking
body:
## Why
Each process held its own float32 copy of every passage vector (665 MB at 164k passages). With one MCP server per Claude session, that exhausted memory and retrieval timed out.

## What
- **Shared vectors.** The vectors are written once as a float16 `.npy` beside the index (`<index>.vectors/`), memory-mapped read-only, and shared by every process through the page cache (336 MB). Scoring widens one 16k-row block at a time, so a query never holds a float32 copy.
- **Fresh across processes.** The copy is named by (count, max id, sum of ids) of the vectors it holds and is checked when `pragma data_version` changes. A paper indexed by another process is now found by dense search without a restart, which was a bug before. Writes are atomic renames, and superseded copies are removed only when older.
- **Hosted models, optional.**
  - `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_API=openai` (the default when the URL ends in `/v1`) uses an OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint. `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_MODEL` stays the index's model identity; `PAPER_FETCH_EMBED_API_MODEL` is the provider's name for it.
  - `PAPER_FETCH_RERANK_URL` uses a Cohere/Jina-style `/rerank` endpoint.
  - Keys come from `*_KEY` or `*_KEY_FILE`. Both stay off unless configured.

## Tested
- 385 tests pass, including new ones: the shared file is mapped by a second index, a writer's new passages are seen by a reader, float16 keeps the top-10 ranking, a read-only location falls back to an in-process copy, and the hosted embedder and reranker accept the common answer shapes.
- Live on the 164k-passage index behind the shared gateway: retrieval 8–12 s warm. The process footprint is 1.6 GB, mostly the ONNX reranker; the vectors are a shared mapped file.

title: Endpoint providers: configured provider by default, cheapest zero-retention first, Near AI support
body:
## What

**Cheapest zero-retention provider first (OpenRouter).** A new setting, `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_SORT`, defaults to `price` and adds `provider.sort` next to `zdr`. For Qwen3.8 27B, OpenRouter then routes to Near AI, at about 1.3¢ per research question instead of about 2.2¢ with load balancing. It falls back to the next zero-retention provider on failure.

**Near AI as a direct provider** (`https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1`, model `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`), for spending prepaid Near AI credits:
- Each call's cost is computed from Near AI's public model list. `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_PRICE` sets prices for any other host that doesn't report cost. An unknown cost is logged as unknown, not zero.
- Run logs name the provider.
- A 402 or credit/balance error says the host may be out of credits.

**The configured provider is the default in the research tool too.** `PIPELINE_MCP_LLM` and `PIPELINE_LLM` now default to `auto`, meaning the configured endpoint when one is set, else the calling model (MCP) or Ollama (CLI). Nothing changes for anyone without an endpoint. `research_start(model="client")` hands one run to the calling assistant when the user asks it to do the writing itself. Replies report `model_backend`, and the gateway's instructions to assistants were updated to match.

Live check through the research tool's own `research_start`/`research_continue` with the real config: the run used the endpoint, handed no tasks to the caller, made 60 calls on zero-retention providers (mostly Near AI) with 0 reasoning tokens, cost 1.3¢ and finished in about 5 minutes.

**`web__search` is listed only when SearXNG is configured.** Without it the tool could only fail, and clients kept calling it. If called anyway, it now explains the fallback: the client searches the web itself and passes the URLs to `papers__leads`. Across 265 runs the web fallback was wanted in 1.2% of searches, so no search engine is required.

**Retries on dropped connections.** Dropped connections and failed TLS handshakes are retried with jittered backoff, up to `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_RETRIES` (default 8).

**No personal paths in code.** `github_mcp` and `patent_mcp` no longer hardcode a home directory. They check the environment variable, then PATH, then `~/.local/bin`.

The docs gain a providers table comparing OpenRouter with Near AI direct, and a cost comparison against renting or buying a GPU.

## Near AI direct: not reliable today

On 2026-10-26, Near AI's API dropped 20–65% of connections during the TLS handshake. Failures rose with parallelism, and all of them came from its single address. Two real research runs failed, the second after one call failed 8 times in a row. Through OpenRouter, the same Near AI-hosted model answered every call. OpenRouter therefore stays the documented default, and Near AI direct is an option.

## Privacy

I scanned tracked files and history for API keys, tokens, emails, home paths and env/key files. Nothing secret was found. The plugin manifests intentionally name the author, with an info@ address, and the public MCP host URL.

## Tests

297 pass. New tests cover the provider default and per-run override, Near AI pricing, the provider label, configured prices, the out-of-credits message and connection retries. Pyright and ruff are clean.

body:
## What

The research pipeline's text model can now run on any OpenAI-compatible chat API (OpenRouter, Fireworks, vLLM, Ollama's `/v1`). It's for research runs that should stay off a hosted assistant. Only the text model moves. Embeddings, the reranker and a configured local verifier (MiniCheck) stay on this machine.

- `Endpoint` in `research_pipeline/llm.py`:
  - Reasoning is off by default (`reasoning: {effort: "none"}`). A model that rejects this is retried with reasoning on, and the run log says so.
  - On OpenRouter, every request carries `provider: {zdr: true}`. Calls go only to zero-retention providers or fail.
  - Answers are requested as `json_schema` and validated against the schema, with one corrected retry. The request falls back to `json_object` if a host rejects `json_schema`.
  - Rate limits and upstream errors are retried with backoff.
- Settings: `PIPELINE_ENDPOINT_URL`, `_MODEL`, `_KEY` / `_KEY_FILE`, `_REASONING`, `_ZDR`, `_CONCURRENCY`. Use `PIPELINE_LLM=endpoint` for the CLI and benchmarks; `PIPELINE_MCP_LLM` now also accepts `endpoint`. **The MCP default stays `client`.**
- The run log records the served model version, the provider, tokens (including reasoning tokens) and cost.
- `eval_pipeline.py` takes `--backend`, `--model` and `--label`, and shows a cost column.

## Model choice

Docs now recommend **`qwen/qwen3.8-27b` as the default** and **`moonshotai/kimi-k3` for important questions**, with `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` as a backup. These come from a comparison on the 4 regression cases: offline, reasoning off, all calls on zero-retention providers.

|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8 27B | 2/4 | yes | ~1.7¢ |
